name: NY-11
label: Safe R

key_factors: Malliotakis's large financial advantage ($2.8M cash vs $35K)
Incumbency advantage with no polling or expert ratings to suggest vulnerability
Prediction markets price Democratic chances at only ~5%
model.rationale: The fundamentals point firmly to Malliotakis: a Republican-leaning district, incumbency, and a roughly 40-to-1 cash advantage over DeCillis. Markets and the absence of any ratings or polling signaling a race both corroborate a comfortable Republican win, so the forecast stays near the baseline with only a modest tightening.
model.watch: Any late polling showing DeCillis within single digits, or a surge of Democratic outside spending, would be the first sign the race is closer than expected.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Nicole Malliotakis seeks a third term in a Staten Island–anchored district that leans Republican by about ten points. She enters the general election with a decisive financial edge, having raised $2.75 million and holding $2.77 million on hand, while Democratic challenger Michael DeCillis has raised under $70,000. No public general-election polls or expert ratings are available for this race, and prediction markets give Democrats only about a five percent chance.

The forecast therefore rests on district fundamentals, which favor the incumbent by a wide margin. A Democratic win would require a substantial anti-incumbent wave well beyond anything visible in the current environment. Malliotakis is a clear favorite, though the lack of polling leaves some room for uncertainty about the exact margin.
